issues: Dolphin is undersized and sits in the upper-middle with a large empty black void to the right and below, so it does not fill the required ~50-60% of display height nor arc across the width, weakening its dominance.
Dolphin body is fragmented: the belly/pectoral region reads as a disconnected blob separated from the main torso by a black gap, breaking the silhouette.
Heavy internal dither makes the dolphin look like scattered noise / a flat bitmap fill rather than a solid lit phosphor form.
No rim light or crisp bright edge on the dolphin, so it lacks the 'lit phosphor object' character the reference demands.
Phosphor glow is flat: individual pixels have almost no soft bloom halo, so the panel reads as plain LEDs rather than an OEL screen.
No persistence / afterglow trails behind the dolphin, so the OEL motion-persistence characteristic is missing entirely.
Bottom-left VU cluster and the bottom segment bar are too bright and busy, competing with the dolphin for attention.
Solid-bright track text at top-left can pull the eye before the dithered (dimmer) dolphin, slightly inverting the intended hierarchy.
suggestions: Scale the dolphin up so its arc spans ~55% of display height and most of the width, eliminating the dead black space on the right and below to make it the unmistakable centerpiece.

Rebuild the dolphin as one contiguous filled body (close the gap to the pectoral/belly region) and add a brighter 1px crisp outline plus a subtle rim-light edge so it reads as a glowing creature, not noise.
Reduce internal dither density and replace with a smoother phosphor fill plus a faint outer gaussian glow layer, keeping the silhouette crisp while giving a true OEL halo.
Add short persistence: 2-3 fading ghost copies of the dolphin trailing its motion path (low alpha, tight decay) to convey OEL afterglow without fogging the scene.
Dim the bottom-left VU segments, the bottom FFT/progress bar, and the right-side telemetry text so they recede below the waves in brightness.
Slightly lower track-text luminance or give the dolphin a touch more peak brightness so the dolphin is the single brightest mass and the eye lands there first.
Add a faint phosphor/scanline texture and a gentle edge vignette over the whole 320x128 frame to sell the physical late-90s OEL panel.
